step: T2 S2 -- the nstp_cap guard decision
why_this_exists: T0_2b Sec 3 rule 3: hitting nstp_cap FAILS LOUDLY and takes a failure edge; it may never pass as
'honest time-stepping'. T0_5 Sec 2.1: nstp_cap is a RESOURCE GUARD, and raising it to MEASURE
uncapped demand is engineering, not a T0 decision -- but 'a capped run is not a feasible run,
whatever the cap is set to'.
So the guard is raised to OBSERVE demand, never to FIT it, and it is fixed and recorded BEFORE
execution. Raising it reactively after a run hits it is fitting the guard to the result.
the_problem: The 2 m identity at cr_target = 0.9 already needed nstp = 2000 -- EXACTLY the cap -- so cr 0.9 may
never have been reached, and its 316 s runtime is a FLOOR. Tightening cr halves dt and doubles nstp,
so the frozen temporal arm at 2 m predicts ~4000 (cr 0.45) and ~8000 (cr 0.225).
Those predictions are built on a base that is itself capped, so TRUE demand may be higher than 8000.

discovery_guard.applies_to: the first uncapped run of any identity whose demand is unknown
rationale: A RUNAWAY guard, not a budget. It is set far above any predicted demand (~5x the ~8000
prediction) precisely so that a legitimate run cannot reach it, while a genuine runaway --
a degenerate velocity field, a mis-specified mesh -- still stops.
Deliberately NOT derived from the capped 316 s run: that base is unreliable, and deriving a
guard from an unreliable base is how the guard ends up fitting the result.

derived_guards.rule: 2x the MEASURED uncapped demand of the same identity at cr_target = 0.9
derived_guards.applies_to: every identity whose cr 0.9 demand has been measured uncapped
rationale: Once true demand is measured the guard can be tight again, because it is anchored on a
measurement rather than a prediction. 2x covers the cr 0.45 -> 0.225 doubling with margin.

rules.uncapped_means: COMPLETED BELOW a predeclared guard -- never 'the guard was removed', and never 'the guard was raised again after it was hit'
rules.on_reaching_a_guard: STOP and escalate. A run that reaches even a raised guard is a FAILURE, not a result -- T0_2b Sec 3 rule 3.
rules.recorded_per_run: the guard the run executed under, and whether it was reached (the artifact's nstp_cap field is already required)
rules.no_reactive_raising: A guard may be raised only BEFORE a run, with the new value and its reason recorded here first.

first_action: Re-run the 2 m identity at cr_target = 0.9 under the discovery guard, to replace the capped 316 s
figure with a real one. That single number decides whether 2 m is affordable at all, which is the
question the lecturer's stated preference for a grid finer than 5 m turns on.
